subject: maths
title: Rounding to the Nearest 10, 100 and 1,000
seo_title: Year 4 Rounding Worksheets: Nearest 10, 100 and 1,000 (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Round any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000; solve number and practical problems that involve all of the above and with increasingly large positive numbers.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths rounding worksheets for the National Curriculum: round to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000 with number lines, halfway numbers, rounding 9s, estimating and word problems. 100 questions with answer key.
key_big: Look one place to the right. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.
key_sub: Then change every digit after the rounding place to 0. A number exactly halfway, such as 450, rounds up. A 9 that rounds up is exchanged: 2,965 to the nearest 100 is 3,000.
body_html:
What rounding means

Rounding finds the closest 10, 100 or 1,000. Rounded numbers are easier to add and subtract in your head, and they help you check whether an answer makes sense.

The rounding rule

  1. Find the digit in the place you are rounding to.
  2. Look at the digit one place to its right.
  3. 5 or more: round up (add 1 to the rounding digit). 4 or less: round down (keep it).
  4. Change every digit to the right of the rounding place to 0.
Round 3,462 to the nearestLook atAnswer
10the ones digit: 23,460
100the tens digit: 63,500
1,000the hundreds digit: 43,000
Exactly halfway

Round 450 to the nearest 100.

450 is exactly halfway between 400 and 500. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up.

Answer: 500

Watch the 9s

Round 2,965 to the nearest 100.

The hundreds digit is 9 and the tens digit is 6, so round up. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds. Exchange 10 hundreds for 1 thousand: 2,900 + 100 = 3,000.

Answer: 3,000

Estimating with rounding

Round each number first, then add or subtract the rounded numbers. Compare the estimate with your exact answer to spot a mistake.

Estimate

Estimate 2,987 + 1,045 by rounding to the nearest 1,000.

2,987 rounds to 3,000 and 1,045 rounds to 1,000. 3,000 + 1,000 = 4,000. The exact answer, 4,032, is close.

Answer: about 4,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding 450 down to 400Exactly halfway rounds up: 500
Changing the wrong digit (3,462 to the nearest 100 = 3,460 or 3,000)Find the hundreds digit first: 3,500
Keeping the digits after the place (3,462 → 3,562)Change every digit after the place to 0: 3,500
Writing 10 in one place (2,965 → 21,000) or losing it (2,965 → 2,000)Exchange 10 hundreds for 1 thousand: 3,000
Rounding twice (6,348 → 6,350 → 6,400)Always round the original number: 6,300

faq.q: What rounding does a Year 4 child need to know?
faq.a: The National Curriculum says Year 4 pupils should round any number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000. They also round decimals with one decimal place to the nearest whole number.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest 1,000?
faq.a: Look at the hundreds digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, round down. So 4,612 rounds to 5,000 and 4,388 rounds to 4,000.
5 rounds up. A number that is exactly halfway, such as 35 or 450, always rounds up, so 35 becomes 40 and 450 becomes 500.

faq.q: Why do children learn to round numbers?
faq.a: Rounding is used to estimate. Estimating before a column addition or subtraction is a quick way to check whether the exact answer is sensible.

items.q: Which number rounds to 450 when you round to the nearest 10?
items.e: Numbers from 445 to 454 round to 450. 447 is in that range. 455 rounds to 460.

items.q: Which number rounds to 800 when you round to the nearest 100?
items.e: Numbers from 750 to 849 round to 800. 763 is in that range. 850 rounds to 900.

items.q: Which number rounds to 1,000 when you round to the nearest 100?
items.e: Numbers from 950 to 1,049 round to 1,000. 972 is in that range. 1,050 rounds to 1,100.

items.q: Which number rounds to 3,000 when you round to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 2,500 to 3,499 round to 3,000. 2,684 is in that range. 3,500 rounds to 4,000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 600 when you round to the nearest 100?
items.e: Numbers from 550 to 649 round to 600. 549 has 4 tens, so it rounds down to 500. The smallest is 550.

items.q: What is the greatest whole number that rounds to 4,000 when you round to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 3,500 to 4,499 round to 4,000. 4,500 has 5 hundreds, so it rounds up to 5,000. The greatest is 4,499.

items.q: Round 6,348 to the nearest 10, the nearest 100 and the nearest 1,000. Which list is correct?
items.e: Always round the number you started with, 6,348. Nearest 10: the ones digit is 8, so 6,350. Nearest 100: the tens digit is 4, so 6,300. Nearest 1,000: the hundreds digit is 3, so 6,000. Do not round 6,350 again to get 6,400.

items.q: Estimate 2,987 + 1,045 by rounding each number to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 2,987 rounds to 3,000 and 1,045 rounds to 1,000. 3,000 + 1,000 = 4,000. (The exact answer is 4,032, so the estimate is close.)

items.q: Estimate 378 + 452 by rounding each number to the nearest 100.

items.e: 6,812 rounds to 6,800 and 2,395 rounds to 2,400. 6,800 − 2,400 = 4,400. (The exact answer is 4,417, so the estimate is close.)

items.q: Estimate 8,730 − 3,214 by rounding each number to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 8,730 rounds to 9,000 and 3,214 rounds to 3,000. 9,000 − 3,000 = 6,000. (The exact answer is 5,516, so the estimate is close.)

items.q: A newspaper says “about 27,000 fans” watched a match. The number was rounded to the nearest 1,000. Which could be the real crowd?
items.e: Numbers from 26,500 to 27,499 round to 27,000. 26,580 is in that range. 26,450 rounds down to 26,000, and 27,500 and 27,900 round up to 28,000.

items.q: A library says it has about 3,000 books, rounded to the nearest 1,000. What is the greatest number of books it could have?
items.e: Numbers from 2,500 to 3,499 round to 3,000. 3,500 rounds up to 4,000, so the greatest is 3,499.

items.q: A museum had 18,463 visitors in March. Which poster shows this number rounded to the nearest 100?
items.e: To the nearest 100, look at the tens digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up to 18,500. 18,460 is to the nearest 10 and 18,000 is to the nearest 1,000.
